📸 Inauguration of the Teletón Rehabilitation and Inclusion Center — Colima, Colima, Oct 6, 2026

🇲🇽✊ "Our Constitution obliges the State to the rehabilitation of people with a permanent disability." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, opening of the Teletón Rehabilitation and Inclusion Center, Colima, Oct 6, 2026 Since December 2024, Article 4 of the Constitution carries two obligations: a scholarship for every person with a permanent disability, and the State's duty to guarantee their rehabilitation, with priority for those under 18. The amendment passed with the support of every political party. The federal government pays the scholarship from age 0 to 29, most states cover 30 to 65, and the universal pension takes over from there. Since 2025 the government has paid Teletón the scholarships of the children it treats.
banner: CONSTITUTION: CHILD REHAB IS A RIGHT

text: 🇲🇽✊ "A space that was once associated with the exercise of power is today destined for the exercise of rights." — Indira Vizcaíno, Governor of Colima, Teletón center opening, Oct 6, 2026 The new Teletón rehabilitation center stands on land that was part of the "Governor's Hacienda" from the late 19th century. Griselda Álvarez, the first woman governor in Mexico's history, turned it into a public park. The center will treat about 700 children and teenagers a year with motor disabilities and autism, from every municipality in Colima and parts of Jalisco and Michoacán. It was built in 228 days. "This collaboration does not replace the responsibilities of public institutions. It complements them."

🇲🇽🛢️ "Electricity is not a common resource. It is a strategic resource... and it cannot be left freely to the market or to international interests." — Luz Elena González, Secretary of Energy, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 Between 2000 and 2020, the State's share of power generation fell to 40%. At times, private generators produced more than CFE. The energy reform made CFE and Pemex public companies again and merged CFE's nine subsidiaries into one. CFE now generates 57% of Mexico's electricity, and the target is 60–61%. Renewables are set to rise from 24% to 38% of generation, and electricity now reaches 99.88% of households after 21,359 electrification works in two years.
banner: ELECTRICITY: NOT LEFT TO THE MARKET

text: 🇲🇽🛢️ "All the countries of the world, all of them: there is not a single one that doesn't have as its goal to seek energy sovereignty." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 Asked about the principles that guide the energy sector after the reform, Sheinbaum listed five. They are energy sovereignty ("that we produce the energy we consume"), sustainability, social justice, national development, and a strong CFE as "a public company of the people of Mexico." Gasoline imports have fallen sharply since 2018, thanks to the Dos Bocas refinery, the Tula and Salina Cruz cokers, and the purchase of the Deer Park refinery. The biggest dependence left is gas: 75% of the natural gas Mexico consumes comes from the United States. That is why solar, wind and geothermal power are being expanded.

🚨🇲🇽 "When I know there is interference, I say it, no problem... And there is a basic principle: respect for our sovereignty." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 El Universal asked about López Obrador's new book. It says US agencies fabricated cases against Sinaloa governor Rubén Rocha and senator Enrique Inzunza, and it calls the capture of Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada an extrajudicial, interventionist US action. Sheinbaum said she has called many US actions interventionist, including before the people at the Monument to the Revolution. She pointed to files declassified by the agencies themselves, among them recently published documents on a US agency's interference around the 1968 student movement. She also noted that much of the family of one of El Chapo's sons was received at the US border: "a fact, not an interpretation."
